# ADR-1092: Package the existing shared disk hygiene hook

## Evidence

The owner requested the existing local shared hook, already used with Claude and
Codex, be packaged in Cortex. The native Codex test used Transartica draft PR #2,
commit ccdf0f9c7b623027d337ca6c094e785308572680. The registered worktree and local
branch were removed after a real push while GitHub retained the commit. Native
SessionStart, Stop and SessionEnd exited successfully. This proves the source
hook's native use, not a later packaged revision.

The owner then specified transcript retention and an opt-in for deletion. A Cortex
SessionEnd receipt records successful session/profile processing; it does not
archive the entire conversation. Transcript deletion removes native resume history.

## Decision

Reuse the existing Python standard-library cleanup implementation, splitting
modules only to meet repository limits. The Codex plugin contains the single
bundle; the full Claude plugin invokes that same bundle through its repository
relative path. No import of the server, database, model or package resolver is needed.

Keep explicit host/session ownership, registration identity, durable evidence,
current remote PR head ancestry, clean/ignored-file checks, process checks and
Git's non-forced deletion. Never delete a remote PR or branch. Workspace cleanup operates
only on registered paths. Host-file cleanup uses explicit ended session IDs and
the existing host-specific selectors. Protect unknown, dirty, replaced, locked and unpushed
work. Git, gh and lsof are external prerequisites; missing checks protect paths.

Retain transcripts by default. CORTEX_CLEANUP_TRANSCRIPTS=delete explicitly enables
the existing host-file deletion behavior; keep is the default and invalid values
fail before deletion. Preserve nested Claude transcripts and file history with
retention enabled. Do not infer deletion consent from a fresh session.

SessionEnd records an ended owner durably before expensive work. Codex's native
three-second limit precludes relying on remote Git checks at that event (ADR-1084).
Startup retries only registered ended owners in the same main repository. A resumed
owner cancels its ended marker. Stop and relevant post-tool events retain immediate
current-owner cleanup. Failures keep pending records, including a branch that could
not be deleted after its worktree was removed. There is no periodic background sweep.

## Verification

Use isolated real Git repositories and fake GitHub responses to cover local/remote
head divergence, ownership, evidence, process and dirty-work protections. Test both
host manifests and transcript retention/deletion explicitly. Keep native host
observations separate from command fixtures. Record before/after counts and checker
results with the final revision. No retrieval benchmark changes are claimed.

## Integration validation

The first PR645 CI run (36257614026, head 3c359821) exposed two consumers omitted
from the initial focused checks: the package inventory contract and the
PostToolUse timing aggregator. The inventory must explicitly include the shared
stdlib bundle. Timing reports must include the cleanup command when configured;
ignoring it would undercount CPU and wall work. Its sample `module` identifier is
`disk_hygiene`; measure that standalone command as configured in the manifest.
The existing report `entrypoint` still describes server-module measurements.
Historical snapshots without that
command remain valid, while unknown or duplicate command hooks remain errors.
Validate package contracts and timing-route tests together with hook behavior.
